newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-JONES LEADS PHOENIX OPEN AFTER FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JONES LEADS PHOENIX OPEN AFTER FIRST ROUND.

text.p: U.S. Open champion Steve Jones barely made it to the tee on time, but then fired a nine-under-par 62 to take a two-stroke lead over Nick Price after the first round of the Phoenix Open on Thursday.
Eight players were tied for third place at five-under 66, including Sweden's Jesper Parnevik and Joe Ozaki of Japan.
Tiger Woods was one of a large group tied at three-under 68.
Jones nearly missed his tee time after miscalculating the time it would take to walk from the range to the first tee.
"I just rushed up there, then hit my three-wood almost out of bounds. Nearly whiffed it," said Jones.
"I ended up making a 12-footer for par. If I can make that first putt on the first hole, I can usually putt pretty well the rest of the day. And that's what happened."
Jones never came that close to bogey in his remaining holes, making birdies on three of his next four and finishing with a total of nine birdies.

For Jones the top priority of 1997 is to earn a spot on the U.S. Ryder Cup team. The top 10 golfers are automatically exempt, and Jones is currently 11th in the standings after picking up points with two top-10 finishes in the last two weeks.
Zimbabwean Nick Price usually skips the West Coast portion of the PGA Tour schedule, but entered this week because he had not played competitively since December 5.
Price made eight birdies and a single bogey, the result of a four-iron in the water on the 12th hole.
"This is my lowest round in a long time," said Price.

"I've been working hard the last few weeks, and really started playing well again last year. I knew if my putting ever came around that I'd be able to really do something. I'm heading in the right direction, which is very exciting for me, because I've still got the desire to excel."
